headline: Athens transforms defunct airport into Europe's largest coastal urban park
meta_description: Two million square meters of former airport land in Athens will become The Ellinikon Park—Europe's largest coastal urban park—designed to cool the city and man…
summary_short: Athens is converting 200 hectares of former airport land into a climate-engineered coastal park that will cool surrounding streets by up to 4°C and open in early 2027.
body:
Two million square meters of former airport land in southern Athens are undergoing a radical transformation into The Ellinikon Park, a 200-hectare coastal urban park designed as a working climate system. Opening in early 2027, it will be Europe's largest coastal urban park—larger than London's Hyde Park and with direct waterfront access along a two-kilometer stretch of the Athenian Riviera. But scale is not what makes it remarkable. Every design choice, from pedestrian paths to water channels, has been engineered to lower local temperatures, manage rainfall completely on site, and sustain more than 520 plant species through sensor-driven irrigation.

The park's design began with thermal mapping and computational fluid dynamics rather than landscaping. Designers ran digital simulations to trace how air moves across the site, then laid out walking routes along natural airflow corridors shaded by strategically placed trees. The result: temperatures along these paths are projected to run up to four degrees Celsius cooler than surrounding streets. Rest areas will maintain more than 60 percent shade while keeping gaps open for ventilation. Water features—channels, misting systems, and basins—function as active cooling infrastructure, while the restored Trachones stream serves both flood protection and water management.

The park achieves full water independence through a wastewater treatment unit producing up to 7,000 cubic meters of treated water daily, plus a 10,000-cubic-meter storage tank for dry periods. Soil and weather sensors continuously adjust irrigation, reducing water use by up to 90 percent compared to conventional systems. Concrete from the demolished airport becomes retaining walls and structural elements; crushed aggregates fill gabions. New surfaces use Greek natural stone selected for both heat performance and visual belonging in the Athenian landscape. The design has been written up as a technical reference for other cities, offering a template rather than a one-time experiment.
quick_facts: 200 hectares—40% larger than London's Hyde Park
Paths designed to be up to 4°C cooler than surrounding streets
Sensor-driven irrigation cuts water use by up to 90 percent
100% of rainfall managed on site with zero runoff
